entries.title: Auto-Document Whole Project
entries.summary: Writes DocInsight documentation into every public declaration a project owns
entries.intro: Read this when a whole project needs documentation coverage instead of symbol-by-symbol work. It writes DocInsight comments into every public declaration the project owns, as a batch of reindex, document and reindex.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Generate & Export > Auto-Document Whole Project...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Generate & Export > Auto-Document Whole Project...
Follow the dialog
The batch reindexes, documents every public declaration the project owns, then reindexes again

surfaces.usage: drag-lint index <path> [--db <file.sqlite>] [--watch [--interval N]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite> ...]

flags.name: --library-db
flags.summary: consult another index for calls THIS one cannot resolve (value receivers typed by name bind too; the manifest key libraryResolve opts a section in).

flags.name: --wait-library
flags.summary: when the platform library of a libraryResolve section is NOT READY, probe every 30 s up to `min` minutes, then continue (marked pending).

flags.name: --require-library
flags.summary: a not-ready platform library is ERROR, exit 2, instead of continuing against the project only.

flags.name: --stall-exit-min
flags.summary: a counter standing still this long ends the run: exit 8, or exit 9 at a quarter of the limit when RAM is critical. A moving counter is never stopped. Off by default.

help: drag-lint index <path>                              [--db <file.sqlite>] [--watch [--interval N]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite> ...] [--wait-library <min>] [--require-library] [--stall-exit-min <min>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>]
--library-db (v21, repeatable): consult another index for calls THIS one cannot resolve.
A hit is recorded by qualified NAME on refs.external_target -- never as a call_edges row,
because target_symbol_id is a NOT NULL FK into this db. A LOCAL answer always wins (the
cross-DB rung runs last), so adding a library can never change an edge that already existed.
Answers only when exactly ONE type and ONE member match; absence beats a guess.
A value receiver typed by NAME binds too (S.Read with S: TStream -> System.Classes.TStream.Read; refs.receiver_type_text
records the type). Without the flag, a manifest section opts in with "libraryResolve": true (default false):
index --all / index --project then open the platform library for the resolve pass only.
WALK SCOPING (any index run): [--exclude-under <dir>]... [--include-only <glob>]...
[--max-file-kb N] [--no-use-ignore] [--no-sql-ms] [--deep|--shallow]
--exclude-under and --include-only are repeatable and prune the walk;
under --project, --exclude-under never drops a compile-closure unit (it names one it kept).
index --project refuses (exit 2) a .dproj under a library-section root, and a library database (library-*.sqlite or a library section's db) as its --db.
--max-file-kb skips a file larger than N KB. --no-use-ignore opts OUT of the
.gitignore / .hgignore pattern files, which are honoured by default. A folder
holding a .scanignore MARKER file (contents never read) is always pruned with
its subtree; --no-use-ignore does not change that. --no-sql-ms indexes EVERY
.sql file, not just the MS*.sql migration scripts CREATE EXCEPTION text is read
from by default. --deep also records usage refs (--shallow is the default).

drag-lint index --project <file.dproj>              [--db <file.sqlite>] [--recompile|--rebuild] [--build-config <Release|Debug|name>] [--no-preprocess] [--dry-run] [--watch [--interval N]] [--wait-library <min>] [--require-library] [--stall-exit-min <min>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>]
[--rule-cache-warm background|wait|off]   after a project index (also each project
section of index --all) the `lint <file>` rule cache is warmed: wait (the default)
in this run; background = in a DETACHED process, so the run returns at once (the
warm recomputes the whole-project rules -- minutes on a large project); off = not at
all. DRAGLINT_RULE_CACHE_WARM=<mode> sets the default. A background warm keeps the
index OPEN until it ends, so a script that deletes the index right after should keep
wait; a newer background warm of the same index stops the older one.
The Done line ends in , parse-errors=N (files parsed this run whose syntax tree had ERROR / MISSING nodes), like the section line (1.51.1).
drag-lint index --scan-libraries-win                [--db <file.sqlite>] [--dry-run]   (Win32+Win64 Library+Browsing paths)
drag-lint index --scan-libraries-all                [--db <file.sqlite>] [--dry-run]   (every platform: +Android/iOS/Linux/OSX)

drag-lint index --all [--config <path>] [--only <Sec1,Sec2>] [--platform win32|win64] [--recompile|--rebuild] [--build-config <Release|Debug|name>] [--dry-run [--json]] [--jobs <n>] [--wait-library <min>] [--require-library] [--stall-exit-min <min>] [--rule-cache-warm background|wait|off] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>]

--wait-library <min>: when the platform library a libraryResolve section binds against is NOT READY (rebuilding, built by an older extractor, schema old, never completed), probe every 30 s up to `min` minutes, then continue; --require-library: a not-ready library is ERROR, exit 2. Default: continue, mark the run pending and say so. The library line is printed before the walk; the platform comes from --platform, the project DB, then the .dproj.
SCAN TYPE is DECLARED BY THE TARGET, not by a flag. --project <.dproj|.dpr|.dpk>
(or a .dpr/.dproj manifest include) indexes the COMPILE CLOSURE: the project
members, the project-local units they transitively use, each one's sibling
.dfm, its {$I} includes, and the project file -- and NOTHING else. A loose
.pas nobody references, and anything on a Delphi Library/Browsing path, stay
OUT. A FOLDER target indexes the whole tree instead.
The scope (closure files, or library folders) is printed CAPPED at 20
entries plus the count; --dry-run lists every entry and indexes nothing.
MODE is CHOSEN PER RUN. [--recompile] (DEFAULT) updates the index in place;
[--rebuild] first empties it of source, then walks. It deletes ROWS, not the
.sqlite: schema, migrations and settings survive and no open handle is
dropped. Implies --force-reparse. The two are mutually exclusive, and BOTH
apply to index --all: each manifest section honours the mode it was given.
[--force-reparse]: re-parse every walked file even when
path+mtime+sha are unchanged. Needed once per DB after an engine upgrade that
extracts something new -- see INBOX 2.3.
EVERY walk SWEEPS, and both halves delete symbols/refs/uses/docs with the
file: PRUNE drops indexed files that left the DISK; EVICTION drops files that
STILL EXIST and left the SCOPE -- a unit dropped from the .dproj, a copy under
an ignored folder, a tree a new [--exclude] now covers. Rows that outlive
their scope make every reference-derived answer (find-callers,
unused-public-symbol, doc facts) wrong. Bounded to the roots THIS run walked,
so indexing one project never purges another's rows from a shared DB, and
reported only when there is something to report. [--prune] forces the sweep
for a single-FILE walk, which does not sweep by default. [--no-prune] is the
one "delete nothing" switch, and it is a DRY LOOK: both sweeps are still
COMPUTED and REPORTED as "would remove" (count + a capped sample of paths),
nothing is deleted. Take it before a big run. Applies to index --all too.
A MALFORMED MANIFEST REFUSES the write (exit 2) -- beside the exe, a local
.drag-lint.json, or --config -- naming the file, the key path and both types
("indexes: expected object, got array"). Read verbs only warn.
A POSITIONAL .dpr/.dproj/.dpk beats the "project" key of the defaults file (one stderr note names the override); an explicit --project beats both.
--use-ignore is the default and is accepted so older scripts still parse; --dir <path> is the same as the positional <path>.
EXIT 1 when any file FAILED to store (an ERROR line on stderr names it and the file keeps its old rows) and, for index --all, when any section failed.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint document --qname <Foo.TBar.Baz> [--profile <name>] [--apply|--json|--format json|--no-backup|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH] - generate/repair a managed DocInsight comment
help: drag-lint document --qname <Foo.TBar.Baz> [--profile <name>] [--apply|--json|--format json|--no-backup|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH]   - generate/repair a managed DocInsight comment

drag-lint document --unit <file.pas> [--apply|--json|--no-backup|--include-accessors|--document-third-party|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH]         - document every public decl in the unit (facts-only; ONE --unit per run: a second, different --unit is exit 2)

drag-lint document --project <p.dpr|.dproj> [--stubs|--apply|--json|--no-backup|--include-accessors|--reindex|--document-third-party|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH]  - document every public decl the project OWNS (--reindex brackets with index: self-freshens so hover/LSP are correct immediately after)
scope: the compile closure restricted to the project's own roots (_D-RAG\drag-lint-project.json, same declaration lint-all reads).
Vendored roots are named and skipped; --document-third-party writes to them too.

entries.title: Custom attributes in the index
entries.summary: Every custom attribute is stored with its argument text and the symbol it decorates (table attributes), library indexes too
entries.intro: Read this when a rule or a query needs to know which declarations carry an RTTI attribute and with which arguments. Each [..] item is one row: attr_name, arg_text, line / col and symbol_id of the decorated class, field, routine, param or property; query it with drag-lint sql.

surfaces.example: drag-lint sql --db <file.sqlite> --query "SELECT a.attr_name, a.arg_text, s.qualified_name FROM attributes a JOIN symbols s ON s.id = a.symbol_id"

entries.title: Include-file indexing and IF evaluation
entries.summary: Include files are indexed under the active build, value defines and IF expressions are evaluated, and an undecidable IF is reported as a pp-unresolved-if hint
entries.intro: Read this when units pull code from .inc files or choose branches with IF directives. The indexer follows includes, evaluates value defines, Declared() and true constants, and says so when it cannot decide a branch.

entries.title: Index a project against its active build config
entries.summary: Parses a project index against the project's active build config (the .dproj Config marker or delphilsp.json) instead of a fixed Release, with an override flag
entries.intro: Read this when a project index must show the code your IDE compiles, for example IFDEF DEBUG branches, or when you want to index a specific build such as Release for a ship view. The index follows the project's active configuration and records it, so a config switch re-parses exactly that database.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint index --project <file.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> [--build-config <Release|Debug|name>]

questions.ask: How do I index my project as the build the IDE has active?
How do I index the Release build while Debug is active?

entries.title: Index DB schema reference
entries.summary: Table-by-table reference of the SQLite index file: every table, column, key, writer pass and schema version 23 to 27
entries.intro: Read this when you query an index with drag-lint sql or need to know which table holds a fact, which pass writes it and since which schema version. The page is checked against drag-lint schema on a live DB.

entries.title: Library bindings for bare reads, paren-less calls and function-result receivers
entries.summary: Bare reads of library vars (Application), paren-less library calls and members on a library function result bind to refs.external_target
entries.intro: Read this when usages shows a library name such as Application as name-only, when a paren-less call of a library function is missing from purity or caller answers, or when a member called on a library function's result (Printer.Canvas, a var inferred from it) has no library target. Since 1.51.1 the resolve pass binds all three and marks a read with refs.external_kind value, parenless-call or proc-value.

entries.title: Library path of the project's Delphi
entries.summary: index reads the library path, IDE variables and $(BDS) from the BDS key of the project's target; a missing key falls back to 37.0 with a one-line note
entries.intro: Read this when a project targets an older Delphi: index follows it for the library path too, so units only that Delphi's Search Path names join the closure and their callers bind.

entries.title: migrate-dbs
entries.summary: Moves project index databases into each project's own D-RAG folder, matching the current index layout
entries.intro: Read this after an index layout change, or when index databases are stranded in an old shared folder. It moves each project index into that project own _D-RAG folder; without --apply it only reports what it would move.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint migrate-dbs [--config <drag-lint.json>] [--apply] move project indexes into each project's _D-RAG folder
help: drag-lint migrate-dbs        [--config <drag-lint.json>] [--apply]   move project indexes into each project's _D-RAG folder
drag-lint --version
drag-lint --help             Accepted AFTER A VERB too: `drag-lint lint --help`,
`drag-lint query find-callers --help` and `drag-lint index --help` all print THIS
banner and exit 0. Until 2026-08-28 every one of those FATALed with exit 3.
Only menu-tree and menu-drift print help of their own; one banner answers every other verb.
Exit reason: an unknown verb (2), unknown flag (3) or stale index (3) also says WHY -- stderr line error[<reason>]:, or with --json a stderr object {"error":"<reason>"}.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Index & Maintenance > Migrate Index DBs to _D-RAG...
steps: drag-lint > Index & Maintenance > Migrate Index DBs to _D-RAG...
Yes applies the move (queued job, LSP stopped); No previews it

entries.title: Per-host bindings for refs in a shared include
entries.summary: A ref inside an include that several units include keeps one binding per host (table ref_host_bindings, schema 26); find-callers and usages read it
entries.intro: Read this when the same .inc is compiled into several units and a name in it means a different declaration in each. The resolver binds such a ref once per host and stores every host's target, so find-callers and usages list the site under each declaration instead of leaving it name-only.

entries.title: pp-profile
entries.summary: Diagnostic that prints the resolved preprocessor define profile for a project, one symbol per line
entries.intro: Read this when you need to know which compiler defines are active for a project, platform and configuration, before trusting a preprocess or index result. It prints the resolved define set, one symbol per line, exactly as the indexer sees it.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint pp-profile [--dproj PATH] [--platform win32|win64] [--config Release|Debug] [--in <file.pas> [--db <file.sqlite>]] (diagnostic: print the resolved define profile, one symbol per line; --in prints the profile of the owning project's active build)
help: drag-lint pp-profile [--dproj PATH] [--platform win32|win64] [--config Release|Debug] [--in <file.pas> [--db <file.sqlite>]]   (diagnostic: print the resolved define profile, one symbol per line; --in prints the profile of the owning project's active build)

entries.title: purge-locals
entries.summary: A size escape hatch for an index database that has grown too large: it drops local-variable and parameter symbols and runs VACUUM to reclaim space
entries.intro: Read this when an index database has grown larger than you want and you do not need per-local symbol lookups right now. It drops local-variable and parameter symbols and runs VACUUM; the call graph is unchanged and the symbols return on the next index.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint purge-locals --db PATH [--json] (size escape hatch: drop skLocalVar/skParam symbols + VACUUM; call graph unchanged; re-inflated on next index)
help: drag-lint purge-locals --db PATH [--json]   (size escape hatch: drop skLocalVar/skParam symbols + VACUUM; call graph unchanged; re-inflated on next index)

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Index & Maintenance > Shrink Index (purge locals)...
steps: drag-lint > Index & Maintenance > Shrink Index (purge locals)...

entries.title: Rebuild Index for This Project
entries.summary: Walks a project's .dproj compile closure and (re)builds its index
entries.intro: Read this after adding or moving units, or when hover, Find Usages or lint results feel stale. It walks the project .dproj compile closure and rebuilds the index for that project.

entries.title: Resolver fixes in 1.52
entries.summary: Generic receivers (`TObjectList<T>.Create`) typed; index --resolve-only without a library keeps the last library bindings
entries.intro: Read this when find-callers misses a call on a generic list or on an element read through a default indexer (also one an ancestor declares, 1.52.3), or when an index --resolve-only run without --library-db used to lose every library binding.

entries.title: schema
entries.summary: Prints the live schema of an index database: schemaversion, every table and column, and row counts
entries.intro: Read this when you need to know exactly what an index database contains before you query it: schema prints the schema version, every table and column, and row counts, read-only.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint schema --db <file.sqlite> [--format text|json] [--output <file>] (self-documenting LIVE index schema: schema_version + tables + columns + row counts, read-only)
help: drag-lint schema --db <file.sqlite> [--format text|json] [--json] [--output <file>]   (self-documenting LIVE index schema: schema_version + tables + columns + row counts, read-only)

drag-lint query --name-like <substring> [--kind class,interface,...] [--limit N] [--json] --db <file.sqlite>   (SUBSTRING search over symbol NAMES -- the discovery query, for when you do not know the identifier yet; ordered shortest-name-first. Distinct from --name, which is exact with an edit-distance fallback)

entries.title: Show Resolved DBs (debug)
entries.summary: Prints which database(s) drag-lint would actually use for a given project, file, or platform, without running a real query
entries.intro: Read this when a query seems to answer from the wrong index: it prints which database(s) drag-lint would use for a project, a file or a platform, without running a real query.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Index & Maintenance > Show Resolved DBs (debug)...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Index & Maintenance > Show Resolved DBs (debug)...
Read the list of databases it would use; no query is run
From a shell: `drag-lint resolve-dbs [--platform win32|win64] [--config <path>] [--json]`

surfaces.usage: drag-lint resolve-dbs [--platform win32|win64] [--repo <file>] [--config <path>] [--json] (print the consumer DB list query/lsp/serve would use)
help: drag-lint resolve-dbs [--platform win32|win64] [--config <path>] [--json]   (print the consumer DB list query/lsp/serve would use)

drag-lint resolve-dbs --project <file.dproj> [--repo <file>] [--config <path>] [--json]   (print the ONE db that owns this project -- the WRITE target; names the field repository it finds, or --repo <file> when given)
exits 2 and names the sections when none or SEVERAL claim the project,
rather than guessing: `index --rebuild` against a wrongly-picked db
clears an index that was never meant to be touched.
drag-lint resolve-dbs --in <file.pas> [--project <file.dproj>] [--config <path>] [--json]
the READ list (what hover / Find Usages / the LSP would open for that
file): the ACTIVE PROJECT's db first, then the folder-matched db.
Omit --project to model "no project active". Same resolution the IDE
uses, so this is how it is verified without an IDE.
No covering index: stdout empty ([] with --json), exit 0, a NOTE on stderr.

pitfalls: never guess a DB path. Also --project `<P.dproj>` and --platform `<win32|win64>`. Read-only: a DB that is not built yet stays on stdout as a bare path, with a stderr NOTE that marks it (missing) and prints the exact index command.

The IDE plugin can add one per-user reference index (since 1.54): %APPDATA%\drag-lint\drag-lint-plugin.ini, section [Databases], keys ReferenceDb (the file) and ReferenceDbFor (a part of the path of the project index it applies to). Missing file, key or database = off; the CLI does not read it.

entries.title: Stable symbol ids on an incremental index
entries.summary: An incremental index keeps the id of every unchanged symbol, so a body edit of a hub unit no longer rebinds every reference to its names
entries.intro: Read this when a one-file incremental index of a widely used unit is slow, or to see what the symbol-id reuse line of the calls stage means.

entries.title: verify-index

entries.title: call-path
entries.summary: Finds the shortest resolved call path from one symbol to another
entries.intro: Read this when you want to know whether routine A ever reaches routine B and how. call-path prints the shortest resolved call path between two symbols, and exits 1 when there is none.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint call-path --from <A> --to <B> [--max-depth N] --db PATH [--json] (shortest resolved call path A -> ... -> B; exit 1 = no path)

entries.title: check-init
entries.summary: Answers whether a variable or field is set before a given use on every execution (SET / NEVER-SET / MAY-BE-UNSET)
entries.intro: Ask it before adding an Assigned guard or reordering initialization: it names the writers of a unit variable, class var or field and says whether one of them runs before the use on every path, with the reason code and the witness when it cannot prove it. Exit 0 = all SET, 1 = some MAY-BE-UNSET or NEVER-SET, 2 = error.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Analyze > Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
steps: Put the caret on a unit variable, class var or field (a use of it) in the code editor
Choose drag-lint > Analyze > Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
The Messages window shows the verdict (SET / NEVER-SET / MAY-BE-UNSET / UNKNOWN-CALLEE), one line per judged use with its witness hops, and one line per writer; double-click a line to jump there

surfaces.caption: drag-lint > Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
steps: Right-click on a variable or field in the code editor
Open the drag-lint submenu and choose Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...

help: drag-lint context            --task "verb qname" [--db <file.sqlite>] [--format md|json|raw] [--no-docs] [--full-surface] [--library-db <library.sqlite>]   (AI-ready symbol bundle: doc + class surface + the target body + capped callers. When the task phrase matches a dl:wiki topic ALIAS, up to 2 topics ride along as a "## Wiki" section -- suppressed by --no-docs. A qname that resolves to nothing now exits 1 and SAYS so)
[--max-callers N] [--context N] [--no-docs] [--max-body-tokens N]

a whole TYPE target keeps its method bodies up to --max-body-tokens estimated tokens (default 20000; 0 = uncapped): a FOCUS method named after the type ("modify TFoo Bar") first, then the most-called-in-type, then the smallest; the rest are listed as header + line range under "## Omitted bodies" (json body_cap, bodies_omitted, omitted_bodies). A member target is never cut (CTX-TYPECAP). When the cap engages, the class surface also drops the member docs of the omitted bodies; a kept body keeps its docs (CTX-SURFACE-DOCS)

the Library calls line also counts the calls whose receiver type the library binds now (json library_calls.via stored|oracle); the library is --library-db or a second --db, else the manifest's for the DB's platform; --library-db none turns that off.

a method reached only THROUGH an interface also gets "## Callers via interface dispatch (IFoo.Bar): N site(s)" sections, after the direct callers; --format json gains "via_dispatch" [{via,kind,sites}] (present only when non-empty) (RB-5)

pitfalls: ~60x leaner than the source. Add --full-surface ONLY for DFM/component/event work.

entries.title: query --kind --all
entries.summary: Lists every symbol of one kind -- every unit, every class, every enum -- with no name, no doc clause and no row cap
entries.intro: Read this when you need the complete set of one kind of symbol, for example every unit in a project or library index to fill a picker. It lists them all with no name and no row cap.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint query --name <symbol-name> [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive] [--exact]
help: drag-lint query              --name  <symbol-name>  [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive] [--exact]
drag-lint query              --qname <qualified>    [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive]
--name/--qname match CASE-INSENSITIVELY (Delphi identifiers are);
--case-sensitive restores byte-exact matching.
--name also accepts a QUALIFIED name (falls back to --qname on a dotted value).
--exact suppresses the fuzzy fallback, so 0 rows means "no such symbol".
JSON rows carry "match_kind": "exact" | "fuzzy" | "substring" (--name-like) -- reject "fuzzy" unless
you want suggestions; a fuzzy row does NOT carry the name you asked for.
--quiet suppresses the "(loaded defaults from ...)" stderr banner.
drag-lint query              --text "<phrase>" [--any-order|--substring] [--source pas|dfm|sql|md] [--kind <k>] [--limit N] [--db ...] [--json]
^ searches STRING LITERALS, DFM/SQL text AND COMMENT PROSE (// { } (* *) ///).
^ a phrase must sit inside ONE string literal / comment: a message built as 'a ' + 'b' over several literals (or lines) is not one phrase -- search one piece, or --any-order.
--source md: Markdown text nodes (headings, paragraphs, list items of the .md files beside a project file).
--kind literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception
narrows it; --kind literal reproduces the pre-comment behaviour exactly.
searches STRING LITERALS ONLY -- string constants, resourcestrings,
DFM captions, SQL exception messages. NOT source text: identifiers,
property assignments and type names are not in this corpus, so 0
matches for those is correct, not a missing index. COMMENTS: doc
comments ARE searchable -- `query find --doc-contains "<phrase>"`.
Only BODY-INLINE comments need grep. (INBOX 2.7; the old line here
sent people to grep for prose the index already had.)

pitfalls: a project DB IS the compile closure, so a hit is membership and a MISS is non-membership.

STRING LITERALS, DFM, SQL *and COMMENT PROSE* -- // { } (* *) and ///. Filter with --kind: literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception. --kind literal is what this returned before comments were indexed.

flags.name: --resolved
flags.summary: precise callers via resolved call_edges (grouped by target, certain|ambiguous); a PROPERTY/FIELD name lists its bound accesses [certain, read|write]; an ENUM VALUE name lists each bound read [certain, read] (resolver 1.6.0-alpha)

flags.name: --json
flags.summary: every row ends with a derived "resolution" key: exact | ambiguous | external | name-only (text totals: N callers (a exact, b name-only)); a site that reaches the target only through an interface method also carries "via", "via_kind" and, for an ambiguous implements edge, "via_edge" (RB-5), placed before "resolution"; with --resolved every row also carries "path" (the full path of the caller file; "file" stays the bare name), before "resolution" (Q-RESOLVED-PATH), and the text rows print (full path:line)

help: drag-lint query find-callers --name  <callee-name>  [--context N] [--resolved] [--db ...] [--json]
--resolved: precise callers via resolved call_edges (grouped by target, certain|ambiguous);
a PROPERTY/FIELD name lists its bound accesses [certain, read|write];
an ENUM VALUE name lists each bound read [certain, read] (resolver 1.6.0-alpha)
EXIT 0 = callers listed, 1 = ZERO callers (a valid answer, not an error;
--json prints []), 2 = usage error or a missing/stale --db. See "Exit codes" below.

--json: every row ends with "resolution": exact|ambiguous|external|name-only (derived; XERJ item 3); --resolved rows also carry "path" = the full path of the caller file ("file" stays the bare name), before "resolution"
a method reached only THROUGH an interface lists those sites as a separate "via IFoo.Bar dispatch" group;
--json rows gain "via" (interface method QName), "via_kind" ("interface") and, when the implements edge is ambiguous, "via_edge" (RB-5)

entries.title: query unit-usage

entries.intro: Read this when cleaning a uses clause or checking an unused-unit-in-uses finding. surfaces.usage: drag-lint query unit-usage --unit <UnitName> [--in <file.pas>] [--db ...] [--json] [--limit N]
help: drag-lint query unit-usage   --unit <UnitName> [--in <file.pas>] [--db ...] [--json] [--limit N]
WITH --in: of that unit's exports, which does THIS file reference? Empty = dead import.
WITHOUT --in: which files reference the unit at all, and which merely IMPORT it.
The candidate set is the uses graph -- in Delphi you cannot name an export without a uses entry.
--limit N (without --in) lists the first N importing files and says how many there are.

pitfalls: omit --in for the project-wide answer; add --in `<F.pas>` to ask about ONE file.

for an RTL/VCL/third-party unit pass the platform library DB too (--db `<proj>` --db `<library>`) for the reference breakdown. With the project DB alone you still get the importer list; only the --in form exits 2.

entries.title: syntax-count
entries.summary: Counts modern syntax in the parse of every unit, uncapped: Delphi 13 if-expressions, is not, not in; inline var/const; anonymous methods; multiline strings
entries.intro: Read this when you want to know how much of a codebase uses a given syntax feature -- for example how many Delphi 13 if-expressions or is-not tests a downgrade would have to rewrite. It parses each unit at the call and counts shapes in the parse, so strings and comments never count and nothing is capped.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint syntax-count (--db <file.sqlite> | --in <path>...) [--feature <a,b>|all] [--per-file] [--hits] [--json]
help: drag-lint syntax-count       (--db <file.sqlite> | --in <path>...) [--feature <a,b>|all] [--per-file] [--hits] [--json]
counts syntax features in the tree-sitter parse of each unit -- shapes, not text, so strings
and comments never count; uncapped. Features: if-expr, is-not, not-in (Delphi 13), inline-var,
inline-const (10.3), anon-method (2009), multiline-string (12); --feature picks some (default all).
--db = every .pas/.dpr/.dpk/.inc row of that index (opened read-only, nothing written);
--in adds a path (repeatable). Text as written: no $IFDEF evaluation, every branch counts.
--per-file lists files with a hit; --hits lists path:line:col per occurrence.
json: features[], files_scanned, files_unreadable, files_with_parse_errors, totals{feature: n},
files[{path, counts}] (--per-file), hits[{feature, path, line, col}] (--hits).
Exit 0 = counted (zero included); 2 = no --db/--in, unknown --feature, unreadable index;
3 = unknown flag.

entries.title: usages
entries.summary: Finds usage sites of a symbol in one of four scopes (this bound symbol, project, group, everywhere), with a choice of report width
entries.intro: Read this when you want every place a symbol is used: usages (also behind Find Usages in the IDE) lists the grouped usage sites. --scope symbol (the default) answers the declaration a position (--in/--line/--col) or a qualified name is bound to; project, group and everywhere widen it to every object of that name in the project, the project group or every index.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint usages --name <X> | --in <file> --line <L> [--col <C>] [--scope symbol|project|group|everywhere] [--group <x.groupproj>] [--width narrow|wide|very-wide] [--db <path>] [--depth N] [--format json|--json] [--limit N] [--rw] [--in <file> [--no-create]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
help: drag-lint usages             --name <X> | --in <file> --line <L> [--col <C>] [--scope symbol|project|group|everywhere] [--group <x.groupproj>] [--width narrow|wide|very-wide] [--db <path>] [--depth N] [--format json|--json] [--limit N] [--rw] [--in <file> [--no-create]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>]
grouped usage report; backs the IDE Symbol Search dialog's Usages view.

--scope (1.52): symbol (default) = the declaration --in/--line/--col or a qualified --name is BOUND to, in this project; project = every object of the name in this project (symbol and project skip a library-*.sqlite --db unless every --db is one); group = the name in every project of --group <x.groupproj>; everywhere = the name in every index the manifest knows. A bare --name with no position binds nothing and is answered as scope project (the JSON says scope, scope_note, databases).
--limit N keeps the first N rows of each JSON group (declarations included) and adds
"limit" and "totals" (the full counts); without it nothing is capped.

--rw: the users of a member split into readers and writers, one block per declaration: a property with its backing field and accessor methods, a field with its properties, a getter (reads) or setter (writes). Rows name the route (property, field, getter, setter, direct).

With no --db, --in <file> finds the unit's project and its database. No DB: prints the index command, exits 2. Two projects list it: names both, exits 2. No project: a library unit on an assumed platform, unless it uses units the library lacks (names them, exits 2). With neither --db nor --in the verb exits 2.

steps: Put the caret on the symbol in the editor
Choose drag-lint > Find Usages...
Read the grouped usage sites

entries.title: uses-recover
entries.summary: Recovers the uses edges of units that ship without source, from the vendor's .hpp headers and a dcc map; never reads a .dcu; --apply stores them in the index
entries.intro: Read this when a project uses a library shipped as compiled units only and you want to know what those units depend on. uses-recover lists every unit the index uses but has no source for, reads its interface uses from the C++Builder header the vendor ships, follows the units those headers name and, given a dcc map, says which the linker pulled in. --project resolves unit aliases first; --apply stores the result so cycles, impact and the uses graph see past the library. No .dcu is read.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint uses-recover --db <db> --hpp-dir <dir>... [--library-db <db>...] [--map <file.map>] [--project <x.dproj>] [--apply] [--json]
help: drag-lint uses-recover       --db <db> --hpp-dir <dir>... [--library-db <db>...] [--map <file.map>] [--project <x.dproj>] [--apply] [--json]
uses edges of units with NO source in --db or any --library-db, from the vendor's C++Builder
.hpp headers (#include lines = interface uses; System/SysInit dropped; never reads a .dcu).
--hpp-dir is repeatable, not recursive, first hit wins; sourceless targets are followed.
--map: a dcc -GS/-GD map; in_map per unit, map_only = linked units no header reaches.
--project: the .dproj's DCC_UnitAlias + the Delphi targets' defaults (WinProcs=Winapi.Windows ...);
a used alias is classified by its target.
--apply WRITES --db: one files row per recovered header (language hpp), its includes as interface
unit_uses rows, then the uses pass binds the project's rows to them; idempotent. Without it: read-only.
json: units[{unit, reach direct|header, used_by, header, in_map, uses[{unit, status
indexed|library|sourceless}]}], no_header[], map_only[], aliases[{unit, to, status}], headers_found,
applied{files, uses, bound} (--apply only).
Exit 0 = reported (zero included); 2 = no --db/--hpp-dir, missing DB/dir/map/project, or --apply on
a stale schema; 3 = unknown flag.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint lint <path> [--rule <id>] [--disable id1,id2] [--rules-dir <dir>] [--json] [--labels] [--no-preprocess] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--build-config <name>]
help: drag-lint lint  <path>       [--profile <name>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>] [--rule <id>|help] [--disable id1,id2] [--rules-dir <dir>] [--json] [--labels] [--no-preprocess] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--build-config <name>] [--no-budget]
[--db <index.sqlite>]  (a store enables the type-aware and ancestry checks, and the project
rules for this file, incl. the ON opt-in discarded-effect-free-result; the OFF opt-in ones run only under --rule)
<path> may be a FOLDER: every scanned .pas/.inc/.dpr gets the same checks as lint <file> (their union)
[--output <file>]: with --json or --format sarif the document is written to the file instead of stdout (a note on stderr).
[--project-rules]  (also run doc-drift/missing-doc for this file -- OFF by default:
they rebuild facts PER DECL, ~16ms each, and can exceed the IDE's 8s budget)
[--stand-in-for <realpath>]  (analyse <path>'s TEXT as though it were <realpath>:
for editor buffers snapshotted to a temp file -- fixes store membership, file id,
unit-name and the reported path)
drag-lint lint  --project <file.dproj> [--build-config <name>] [--rule unit-not-in-dpr|unit-not-in-library|help] [--json]
drag-lint lint  --in <f.pas> --fix [--fix-line <L> --fix-rule <id>] [--fix-naming] [--apply [--no-backup]]   (AUTOFIX one file; --apply keeps a .bak beside each file it writes unless --no-backup)
DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply: it reports what it would change and writes no source file.
--fix-line + --fix-rule together narrow the fix to ONE finding; omit both to
apply every fixable finding in the file. Only rules whose catalog entry has
"fixable": true are ever applied -- see `drag-lint rules --json`.
--fix-naming: kept for compatibility, a no-op since 1.37.0 -- every fix, the naming renames (across
every owning project) included, is ON by default; only "autofix_off": [...] in drag-lint-lint.json withholds one;
with it the run still prints "rename-local: <N>" (stderr) for the single-project renames.
This is what the IDE Structure form's right-click Fix it / Fix all in unit run.

entries.title: exceptions-sync
entries.summary: Declare one exception class per distinct raise Exception.Create message, then rewrite the raise sites
entries.intro: Read this when a project raises bare Exception.Create with literal messages and you want one named exception class per distinct message. It is opt-in: add an "exceptions" block to drag-lint-lint.json (an empty one is enough; without it the verb says the feature is off and exits 0). It runs as a dry run, and --apply writes the classes into a managed block in your exceptions unit; the raise sites are then rewritten by `drag-lint lint <file> --fix --fix-rule raise-bare-exception [--apply]`.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint exceptions-sync [--profile <name>] [--db <file.sqlite>] [--config <lint.json>] [--apply] [--json] (materialise the project's derived exception classes)
help: drag-lint exceptions-sync    [--profile <name>] [--db <file.sqlite>] [--config <lint.json>] [--apply] [--json]   (materialise the project's derived exception classes)
Harvests every bare `raise Exception.Create('literal')` in the project and declares one class per
DISTINCT message inside a drag-lint:auto managed block in the exceptions unit. DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply.
Opt in with an "exceptions" block in drag-lint-lint.json -- an empty one is enough; key "unit" names
the unit (default uExceptionDefinitions, created if absent) and key "root" the ancestor (default Exception).
Each declaration carries its message in a same-line // comment, and THAT COMMENT IS THE KEY: rename a
generated class freely, but edit its comment and the next run adds a second class for the old message.
It is a VERB and not a --fix because its input is project-wide and its output is one file; the CALL-SITE
rewrite is the fix-it half and lives on `lint <file> --fix --fix-rule raise-bare-exception [--apply]`.

flags.name: --quiet
flags.summary: suppress per-file progress lines written to stderr

help: drag-lint lint-all           [--profile <name>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>] [--db <file.sqlite>] [--project <.dproj>] [--build-config <name>] [--rule <id>[,<id>...]] [--disable id,...] [--output <report.txt>] [--json] [--labels] [--quiet] [--lint-third-party] [--no-preprocess] [--shared-db <db> ...] [--library-db none] [--no-budget]

--output <file>: the text report goes to the file (default lint-report-YYYYMMDD.txt beside --project, else beside the DB); with --json or --format sarif the JSON / SARIF document does instead (a note on stderr, stdout stays empty).
--fix [--fix-naming] [--apply]: autofix every unit, as lint --fix (dry run without --apply)
--rule <id>[,<id>...]: RUN and report ONLY those rules (1.51.1: a comma list narrows execution and derives no --shared-db peers, as one id does); naming an OFF-by-default rule opts it in
for the run (no --enable needed) -- the same contract as lint and lint-project.
--quiet: suppress per-file progress lines written to stderr

on a --db the manifest does not register (a copy), the dl:shared marker-peer pass is skipped with one stderr note and sibling DBs resolve to same-named copies beside --db (else could not check); --shared-db <db> still runs (1.51.1).
--project <.dproj|.dpr>: report ONLY on the units that project compiles
(its compile closure + their .dfm siblings). Use it when one folder holds
several projects, or when the DB spans more than the project you are reviewing.
taint-sql-injection / taint-command-injection / taint-path-traversal (store-backed): walk the index's data_flows
facts from a catalogued source to a sink; catalogues rules\taint-sources|sinks|propagators.json, extended by the
"taint" object of drag-lint-lint.json: sources sinks propagators sanitizers disable max_depth lib_depth max_rounds
follow_ambiguous weak_receiver_regex weak_severity_drop max_paths_per_sink second_order.
--fix [--apply]: AUTOFIX every fixable finding across the whole project.
DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply. This is what the Structure form's right-click
"Fix all in project" runs. It can rewrite many files at once -- dry-run first.

pitfalls: lint `<file>` is a strict SUBSET: project-wide rules can only fire in lint-all.

flags.summary: measurement runs: open no stand-down channel, so a maintenance stand-down from another process cannot cut the run to PARTIAL (exit 4)

flags.summary: another project index, repeatable: evidence for a closure-dependent dl:ok on a dl:shared unit

pitfalls: A second --db is the library slot, not another project: to judge a dl:ok on a dl:shared unit use --shared-db.

`--library-db <lib>` names the library slot too and wins over a second --db and the manifest; a missing file refuses (exit 2), `none` means no library. Without a library, a type whose ancestry lives there stays unknown and the type-aware rules stay silent on it.
lint `<file>` is a strict SUBSET: project-wide rules can only fire in lint-all.
A vendored folder INSIDE the project folder is linted as your own code until `excludeRoots` names it in `<project>\_D-RAG\drag-lint-project.json`.

entries.title: document-all
entries.summary: Documents every public declaration in every indexed unit, with no project scope
entries.intro: Read this when you want to sweep DocInsight comments across everything in the index rather than one project at a time. document-all documents every public declaration in every indexed unit; the default is facts-only. Without --apply it is a dry run (it prints the edits and writes nothing); with --apply it writes the comments, with a .bak unless --no-backup. Exit 0 on success including a dry run, 1 when some edits were refused because the index was stale (reindex, then re-run), 2 on a usage or database error.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint document-all [--profile <name>] [--stubs|--apply|--json|--format json|--no-backup|--include-accessors|--document-third-party|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH] - document every public decl in every indexed unit (no project scope)
help: drag-lint document-all [--profile <name>] [--stubs|--apply|--json|--format json|--no-backup|--include-accessors|--document-third-party|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH]               - document every public decl in every indexed unit (no project scope)

batch modes (--unit/--project/document-all) default facts-only: an empty tag is never written, <param> never gets a skeleton, and <summary> appears only when harvested from a nearby // comment; add --stubs to keep a fresh comment that has no facts block
batch modes also skip TRIVIAL Get*/Set* property accessors (impl body <= docs.accessor_trivial_max_lines, default 2) by default; add --include-accessors to document them too
drag-lint document --unit <file.pas> --strip [--apply|--no-backup] [--db PATH]   - REMOVE drag-lint-generated doc tags/blocks (marker-keyed; hand-written docs untouched)
--strip is also accepted on --qname/--project/document-all (strips just that symbol's doc region, or every file in scope); mutually exclusive with --stubs
<seealso cref> links to related symbols (callees + siblings) are emitted BY DEFAULT in every document mode;
--no-seealso turns them off. (--seealso is still accepted and does nothing -- it was the opt-in before it became the default.)
add --since [--base-dir <repoRoot>] to emit a git-derived <since> date; degrades silently when git is absent
@deprecated is auto-detected from the Pascal 'deprecated' directive on the decl -- no flag needed
--migrate-pure: regenerate a stored legacy <para>Pure</para> fact (purity v1). Without it a block whose ONLY difference is that line is left byte-identical, and doc-drift agrees
PROJECT TAGS: on a block reconciled across projects (dl:shared, or holding facts this index cannot see) the inbound entries -- Called from:, Used by:, Used in units:, Covered by: --
carry the projects that rendered them: Called from: [DataCopy,DataCopyTests]uX.Foo (uX.pas). A run adds/removes only ITS tag (the project's name, recorded in the index;
the DB base name for indexes built before 1.18.0); an entry goes when its set empties; untagged legacy entries keep the old rules

entries.title: Lint --fix through the compile gate

entries.intro: Read this before letting lint --fix write into a project you cannot afford to break. entries.title: Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)
entries.summary: Lists every unit a project uses that is neither a project member nor in the library, judges each one (project unit or third-party) and fixes it either way
entries.intro: Read this after moving or adding units by hand, or when lint reports unit-not-in-dpr or unit-not-in-library. surfaces.usage: drag-lint reconcile-project <App.dpr|.dproj> [--apply] [--to project|library] [--only <unit,...>] [--db <db>] [--full] [--json] [--config <path>] - sync project member list; flag stale used units. --only restricts MISSING (and therefore --apply) to a reviewed selection, so a dry run with --only previews exactly what --apply would write. --json carries `applied` (the OUTCOME, false when --apply had nothing to write) plus `backups` and `edited` when --apply is passed. MISSING = used units neither listed nor in the library (registry library path or the manifest library section's include); each is judged by the project's own roots: project unit (fix --apply) or third-party (fix --apply --to library, which adds its folder to that include in --config or the exe-dir drag-lint.json, .bak first). --json items carry owner, suggestedFix and folder

entries.title: convert-apply #migrate (member, type and enum rename / DL_NONE)
entries.summary: #migrate renames or DL_NONE-breaks a member at its .pas access sites; at file scope (or with a uses unit) it renames a type, enum or identifier
entries.intro: Read this when a component conversion changes the names of methods, events or properties the code uses. Inside a #convert block, #migrate Old -> New renames the member at every bound access site in the .pas; Old -> DL_NONE marks the site for hand conversion instead. A #migrate at file scope (or naming a uses unit) renames a type or enum identifier in the code -- declarations, casts, is/as, generic arguments, enum literals -- maps enum members by name, adds the new unit to uses, and warns on every site it does not rename.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint convert-apply --unit <F.pas> [--unit <G.pas> ...] --rules <file> --db PATH [--db ...] [--only Name1,Name2,...] [--castlib <file>] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--no-warn-unlinked] [--no-reconcile-uses] [--no-reindex] [--old-platform-db <file> ...] [--format json|--json] (locates .dfm component instances matching a #convert rule and rewrites all 5 surfaces: declaration retype + uses-add + .dfm re-emit + property/event access-site rewrite + runtime-creator retype/TODO markers; without --apply this is DRY-RUN ONLY (preview, writes nothing); --apply writes for real with backups + a recovery.txt unless --no-backup; --format json emits schema apply/1 -- the six report surfaces plus a typed items[] carrying a machine-readable kind per line, so the conversion REMAINDER can be dispatched on instead of parsed out of prose, plus resolved_defaults[] (informational receipts, kept OUT of items[] because on a real form they run to thousands and would bury the remainder); --castlib names the .castlib whose enum blocks translate a #link value when the link carries a cast suffix; a source property some converted instance carries that no #link carries and no #ignore acknowledges is warned ONCE per (source type, property) as "dropped on N of M converted instance(s)" -- a minority count is the stronger signal -- and counted in json as unlinked_source_properties / unlinked_source_property_sites / unlinked[]; --no-warn-unlinked drops the warnings and keeps the count; the book's UNIT rules act on the unit too: #unuse Old removes it, #use New adds it to the implementation uses when absent from both clauses, #useswap Old -> New1[, New2] removes Old and adds each New once into the section Old was in (a unit that does not use Old gets no edit from the swap) -- a unit both added and removed is kept, an entry inside a {$IF...} region refuses the unit (exit 1, nothing written); with no sibling .dfm, no #convert block or no matching instance the unit rules run alone (component part skipped; a book with no unit rules still needs the .dfm, exit 1); json adds component_part, uses[] {action,unit,section,line,rule,reason}, uses_removed, uses_added; the To type's unit goes to the INTERFACE uses when the retyped field is declared in the interface, and is MOVED there from an implementation-only use (1.23.0);EVERY #convert block is validated and freshness-checked -- each #link/#default against its own From/To types, each #mapping against the blocks that #apply it -- with each path resolved segment by segment, no depth limit (a published leaf; each hop published, or public and class-typed; private never); a #convert type that resolves in no --db REFUSES the unit, dry run and --apply alike -- an index gap, not a rule error ('<Type> (line N) resolves in no --db -- index gap in the library or project index; reindex, or report it, before converting'); json classes_built counts the classes whose members were resolved; a #link/#default/#mapping path through a member that exists but is inaccessible is SKIPPED, never applied and never an error -- the unit converts the rest -- and reported as a 'line N: warning: ...' line (text: under Warnings; json: warnings[] strings, items[] kind rule-path-unreachable, and unreachable[] {line,path,member,visibility,class,reason,message}); an inherited/inline .dfm object of a From type whose declaring ancestor is not converted is SKIPPED, never converted, while the unit's own instances, code and unit rules convert (1.22.0) -- each reported as a 'line N: warning: ...' line (json: warnings[], items[] kind inherited-instance-skipped, and inherited[] {name,type,line,ancestor_unit,ancestor_state,reason,action}; ancestor_state unconverted|converted|mismatched|outside: the declaring ancestor -- the nearest ancestor class whose .dfm opens it with object -- still has the From type, already has the To type, has a third type, or is not determinable: in no --db, or an ancestor .dfm on the way is missing or binary, which stops the walk; --only filters inherited[] too); one whose declaring ancestor ALREADY has the To type is RETYPED (1.26.0, C8 N2): inherited X: TFrom -> inherited X: TTo, keyword kept, nested and inline-frame children too; the properties its block overrides convert per the book (what it does not stream it inherits: no default resolved, no #default written); its code access sites are rewritten as for an own instance and the To unit is added; every code access to a field a converted ancestor declares (bound by the resolver, any level up) is rewritten too, .dfm block or not (N2a) -- json inherited[].action retyped|code|skipped|unverified (code: line = its first .pas reference), a converted[] line and items[] kind inherited-instance-retyped, not a warning; --only filters both; info capability inherited_retype; a code-only use of an UNCONVERTED ancestor's field is listed as action skipped, ancestor_state unconverted, reason 'ancestor not converted' (1.26.7, capability inherited_code_unconverted); the book's #warn <FromPath> "<text>" fires once per converted instance whose SOURCE .dfm streams FromPath (<value>, <name>, {Prop} expanded) -- 'line N: warning: <inst>: <text>', items[] kind book-warning with value; #check-ref <ToPath> <Class>.<Prop>[, ...] warns when the converted ToPath value contains \ or : (ref-path-like) or no listed Class.Prop of any .dfm in the project index carries it (ref-dangling), and once per run ref-not-checked when the index holds no .dfm property facts; info capabilities book_warn, check_ref (1.26.5); every code rewrite is scoped to the instance's field (receiver bound to it, or unbound / bare / Self. in a routine of the .dfm root class with no same-named local); a site the index cannot vouch for is NOT rewritten and is reported ('access site <file>:<line> ... not verified against the index -- not rewritten', items[] kind access-site-unverified, json access_sites_unverified); a --db resolved before resolver 1.12.0 is REFUSED, dry run too, naming the index ... --resolve-only fix; a #link carrying a cast never rewrites a .pas access site (1.27.0, interim): the cast's pas template is a statement with no correct splice inside an expression, so each bound site is reported -- 'line N: #link To <- From : Cast -- access site <file>:<line> <inst>.<From> not rewritten: ... convert this access site by hand', items[] kind cast-not-applied with instance, file, line and value (the cast); no .pas edit, the .dfm half of the cast unchanged; kind cast-applied is retired; info capability cast_site_refusal; a VALUE cast -- a castlib block with 'value strip-db' (shipped: StripDB, #link TableName <- TableName : StripDB) -- removes one trailing .db, any case, from the linked string: in the .dfm of each converted instance, and in .pas assignments whose right-hand side is ONE string literal; any other assignment and every read get no edit and a warning (items[] value-cast-applied {old_value,value} / value-cast-check; text 'value casts: N value(s) changed ...'); an unknown value keyword fails the run; entries.title: convert-apply
entries.summary: Locates .dfm component instances that match a #convert rule from a conversion-rules file and rewrites all five surfaces: declaration retype, uses-add
entries.intro: Convert the forms and units that use an old component to its replacement, by the rules in a conversion-rules book. Preview first; add --apply to write.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint convert-apply --unit <F.pas> [--unit <G.pas> ...] --rules <file> --db PATH [--db ...] [--only Name1,Name2,...] [--only-type Type1,Type2] [--castlib <file>] [--glyph-stitch] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--raise-encoding "<path>=utf8-bom" ...] [--no-warn-unlinked] [--no-reconcile-uses] [--no-reindex] [--old-platform-db <file> ...] [--progress] [--format json|--json] (locates .dfm component instances matching a #convert rule and rewrites all 5 surfaces: declaration retype + uses-add + .dfm re-emit + property/event access-site rewrite + runtime-creator retype/TODO markers; ancestor_state unconverted|converted|mismatched|outside: the declaring ancestor -- the nearest ancestor class whose .dfm opens it with object -- still has the From type, already has the To type, has a third type, or is not determinable: in no --db, or an ancestor .dfm on the way is missing or binary, which stops the walk; --only filters inherited[] too); one whose declaring ancestor ALREADY has the To type is RETYPED (1.26.0, C8 N2): inherited X: TFrom -> inherited X: TTo, keyword kept, nested and inline-frame children too; the properties its block overrides convert per the book (what it does not stream it inherits: no default resolved, no #default written); its code access sites are rewritten as for an own instance and the To unit is added; every code access to a field a converted ancestor declares (bound by the resolver, any level up) is rewritten too, .dfm block or not (N2a) -- json inherited[].action retyped|code|skipped|unverified (code: line = its first .pas reference), a converted[] line and items[] kind inherited-instance-retyped, not a warning; --only filters both; info capability inherited_retype; a code-only use of an UNCONVERTED ancestor's field is listed as action skipped, ancestor_state unconverted, reason 'ancestor not converted' (1.26.7, capability inherited_code_unconverted); the book's #warn <FromPath> "<text>" fires once per converted instance whose SOURCE .dfm streams FromPath (<value>, <name>, {Prop} expanded) -- 'line N: warning: <inst>: <text>', items[] kind book-warning with value; #check-ref <ToPath> <Class>.<Prop>[, ...] warns when the converted ToPath value contains \ or : (ref-path-like) or no listed Class.Prop of any .dfm in the project index carries it (ref-dangling), and once per run ref-not-checked when the index holds no .dfm property facts; info capabilities book_warn, check_ref (1.26.5); every code rewrite is scoped to the instance's field (receiver bound to it, or unbound / bare / Self. in a routine of the .dfm root class with no same-named local); a site the index cannot vouch for is NOT rewritten and is reported ('access site <file>:<line> ... not verified against the index -- not rewritten', items[] kind access-site-unverified, json access_sites_unverified); a --db resolved before resolver 1.12.0 is REFUSED, dry run too, naming the index ... --resolve-only fix; a #link carrying a cast never rewrites a .pas access site (1.27.0, interim): the cast's pas template is a statement with no correct splice inside an expression, so each bound site is reported -- 'line N: #link To <- From : Cast -- access site <file>:<line> <inst>.<From> not rewritten: ... convert this access site by hand', items[] kind cast-not-applied with instance, file, line and value (the cast); no .pas edit, the .dfm half of the cast unchanged; kind cast-applied is retired; info capability cast_site_refusal; a VALUE cast -- a castlib block with 'value strip-db' (shipped: StripDB, #link TableName <- TableName : StripDB) -- removes one trailing .db, any case, from the linked string: in the .dfm of each converted instance, and in .pas assignments whose right-hand side is ONE string literal; any other assignment and every read get no edit and a warning (items[] value-cast-applied {old_value,value} / value-cast-check; text 'value casts: N value(s) changed ...'); an unknown value keyword fails the run; info capability value_cast_strip_db (1.27.0); json pas_uses[] (1.27.0, dry run and --apply; info capability pas_uses) lists what the .pas still uses that the map does not cover: one row per (instance, member) the code reaches through a converted instance -- the access-site rewrite's own bound sites -- and one per global (routine/const/var/type) from a unit the reconciliation removes: {instance,from_type,to_type,member,kind method|property|field|event|const|var|type|routine|enum-value,visibility,declaring_unit,declared_in,status mapped|cast-refused|same-name|unmapped|global-dangling,lines[],count,resolution resolved|ambiguous|class-not-found|member-not-found|kind-unknown,candidates[]}; the From class is resolved through the unit's scope (the unit itself, then the LAST uses entry declaring it, then the book's qualified #convert From, then a lone declarer) -- several declarers left over is resolution ambiguous with candidates[] units and empty kind/declarer, never a pick (1.28.2, info capability pas_uses_resolution); text prints 'pas uses: N unmapped, M global-dangling, K same-name, J mapped, C cast-refused' and one line per unmapped member; a DESCENDANT unit (a class descending from the unit's root class at any level, or a form hosting it inline) that still streams a converted instance in its .dfm or uses it in code is a WARNING, never a refusal (1.25.0): 'line N: warning: descendant <Unit> still streams <Name> as <TOld> -- convert it next (needs C8 N2)', N = the instance's object line in this .dfm (json: items[] kind descendant-not-converted, descendants[] {unit,name,type,line,reason}; line = the descendant .dfm block, else its first code reference; reason dfm|code|both; --only filters it; only descendants the --db index are seen); a plan the edit applier would refuse in part (overlapping delete ranges -- an engine defect) fails the WHOLE unit before anything is written, dry run too, and a write that fails part-way is ROLLED BACK byte-identical (exit 2, '-- rolled back, unit not changed'; a failed rollback names the files it could not restore) (1.25.1): exit 1, 'ERROR: refused N edit(s) to <file> -- overlapping delete ranges (an engine defect) -- unit not changed, nothing written', json ok=false with that error; a .dfm component nested in another converted one is spliced into its parent's re-emit, and --only naming the parent converts it too (json only_included[] {name,parent}, text '--only: <child> converts too -- nested in <parent>'); a collection property (FieldDefs = < item ... end>) whose item members the book links (#link X.Items.* <- X.Items.*, identity) is carried whole when the To type publishes X with the same collection type, else reported NOT carried with its item count and counted as dropped, #ignore X notwithstanding; a deliberate refusal writes nothing and prints one 'REFUSED: <reason>' line -- a uses entry to change inside a {$IF...} region; an instance whose indexed .dfm span no longer holds it (lines added or removed, a block shrunk onto a sibling's end, or the .dfm cut short: '<Name>: index is stale for this .dfm -- reindex'); a #unuse / #useswap removing the unit that declares the From type of an instance left unconverted (skipped, inherited/inline, or excluded by --only) is refused too ('<rule> would leave <N> unconverted instance(s) of <Type> -- unit not changed') -- EXCEPT that with --only, when every such instance is one --only left out, the removal is SKIPPED (1.23.0: unit kept; json uses[] action skipped with a reason, a 'line N: warning:' line, items[] kind unit-rule-skipped; info capability only_skips_unit_rules); USES RECONCILIATION (1.27.0, C9, default on; --no-reconcile-uses = the 1.26.6 rules above, exactly): the converted .pas/.dfm are RE-INDEXED IN MEMORY (the indexer's own extractor, no DB written, so the dry run shows the --apply plan) and every #unuse / #useswap Old is a WATCH LIST -- the unit is KEPT while a component the converted .dfm still streams has a class declared in it (an unconverted instance, a second component type of that unit, an inherited instance the ancestor has not converted: R26's refusal becomes this, the --only skipped row is unchanged), REMOVED when only .pas code needs it (its dangling references named, the compile errors are the signal), KEPT when no --db indexes it; presence is scope-alias aware (#unuse DBTables matches Bde.DBTables, #use DB is satisfied by Data.DB); a bare name the conversion INTRODUCES into the .pas gets its declaring unit added -- interface uses when referenced above implementation -- and a name (or To type) two units declare is REPORTED, never picked (add #use <unit> to choose); a To-type tie the book's #use (or a uses entry of the unit) settles takes that unit, into the INTERFACE uses when the retyped field is declared there, or MOVED there (C9 A8-1); the C13 move is a row; every unit the #convert surface adds (a To type's unit, a #convert header's trailing unit) is an add row too (rule #convert, source rule, counted by uses_added; none when already present); json: uses[] action remove|add|skipped|kept|moved with source rule|reconcile|convert and needed_by[] {name,line,section}, uses_kept, uses_moved, uses_unresolved[] {name,line,section,reason ambiguous|not-found,candidates[] {unit,db}}, uses_reconcile on|off|degraded, items[] kinds unit-rule-kept, unit-rule-dangling, unit-rule-unverified, uses-unit-ambiguous (all warnings); after --apply the unit's OWN project DB -- the one --db that indexes it, a project index holding one .dproj/.dpr -- is refreshed with 'index --project <it> --db <it>' in a child process (json uses_reindex {status done|skipped|failed|dry-run|off,db,project,ms,reason}; a child still running after 10 minutes is terminated: failed; --no-reindex skips it; no other DB is ever written); info capability uses_reconcile; inside a #convert block '#migrate Old -> New' renames the member at every bound .pas access site of the block's converted instances (methods, events, properties; json items[] migrate-applied) and '#migrate Old -> DL_NONE' wraps each site, inst.Old -> DL_NONE(inst.Old), a deliberate break that does not compile until converted by hand (items[] deliberate-break, field todos); both make pas_uses[] status mapped; a with block, an unverified receiver, a scoped / template form or a member a #link already converts is never rewritten (items[] migrate-check); info capability migrate_members (C18 slice 1); an IDENTIFIER #migrate (file scope, or in a block naming uses units or an enum-value target; 1.38) renames every bare Old token in the .pas code -- var/param/field/result types, casts, is/as, generic arguments, enum literals; never comments or strings -- when New resolves in a --db (else items[] migrate-check per site plus one rule-level, line 0, per rule -- the editor marks the book line; no rename), maps an enum type pair member by member on the name after the lowercase prefix (an explicit #migrate member line overrides; an unmatched member in use is a migrate-check; --old-platform-db <file>, repeatable, 1.43, names the index of the platform the code was written against: the From enum's members are read from it first and today's --db members added, an enum only it declares maps too, it never answers for a target, and an unreadable one exits 2; info capability old_platform_enum_map), never renames a qualified Unit.Old site (migrate-check), and adds the unit declaring New to uses (interface uses when a site is there), on a unit with no sibling .dfm or no matching instance too (1.42; component part skipped); info capability migrate_identifiers; --only names match case-insensitively; a name matching no #convert instance is ignored, never an error, and reported (json only_matched[] / only_unmatched[], always present; text '--only: no #convert instance named X (ignored)'); --unit may repeat (1.23.0): every unit runs in ONE process sharing one rule-book validation and one member cache -- text: one '=== unit i of N: <path> ===' section per unit, then 'batch: N unit(s) -- a ok, b refused, c failed; classes_built K; exit E'; json: ONE apply-batch/1 document {mode,rules_file,units_count,ok,exit_code,ok_count,refused_count,failed_count,classes_built (the run total),units[]: one apply/1 per unit, each equal to that unit's single run -- its classes_built is the unit's own}; under --apply a file a unit cannot write fails that unit before anything is written (exit 2); a unit's refusal or failure never stops the others; exit = the worst unit's; 1.42: the batch RUNS ancestor-first -- a unit runs after every unit of the run that declares one of its inherited / inline .dfm objects (owner ruling Q5), so --apply retypes them; units[] stays in --unit order; text prints 'convert-apply: units run ancestor-first: <names>' when the order changed; info capability batch_units; 1.33.0: every apply/1 (single or units[]) carries exit_code (that unit's); entries.title: convert-scaffold
entries.summary: Auto-generates a valid conversion-rules file from the real property trees of a from-type and a to-type
entries.intro: Generate a starting conversion-rules book for a pair of component classes, from their real property trees, instead of typing every rule.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint convert-scaffold --from <FromType> --to <ToType> [--output <file>] [--surface dfm|pas] [--depth N] [--rules <file>] [--progress-interval S] --db PATH [--db ...] (auto-generate a VALID conversion-rules file from the real F/T property trees, expanded to --depth N, else the --rules book's #depth N, else 5 (a bad value exits 2): concrete #link where 1 source matches by leaf-name+type, ??? for ambiguities, DROPPED notes for orphaned F props; --surface picks the TO-side target bar, default dfm=published-properties-only, pas=published+public incl. public fields; is_writable=false targets are never auto-linked on either surface; --progress-interval S: see PROGRESS below)
help: drag-lint convert-scaffold --from <FromType> --to <ToType> [--output <file>] [--surface dfm|pas] [--depth N] [--rules <file>] [--progress-interval S] --db PATH [--db ...]   (auto-generate a VALID conversion-rules file from the real F/T property trees, expanded to --depth N, else the --rules book's #depth N, else 5 (a bad value exits 2): concrete #link where 1 source matches by leaf-name+type, ??? for ambiguities, DROPPED notes for orphaned F props; --surface picks the TO-side target bar, default dfm=published-properties-only, pas=published+public incl. public fields; is_writable=false targets are never auto-linked on either surface; --progress-interval S: see PROGRESS below)

PROGRESS (proptree, convert-scaffold): --progress-interval S (whole seconds; default 0 = OFF) writes one JSON line to STDERR at most every S seconds while the tree is built -- {"progress":{"elapsed_s":12.3,"verb":"proptree","class":"<qname>","depth":2,"max_depth":5,"classes_done":41,"classes_queued":7,"nodes":3114}} -- stdout is unchanged; S not decimal digits (x, -1, +3) or missing exits 2; every stderr line is flushed BEFORE the stdout document, which is written in one piece (a merged pipe reads notes, then the whole document); convert-apply / convert-validate reject --progress-interval as an unknown argument (exit 3) -- convert-apply takes --progress instead (1.33.0: one line per finished unit, see convert-apply); cancel = kill the process (the default write-back is kill-safe: each memoized type is its own SQLite statement)

questions.ask: Why does Convert reorder my units, or refuse because of an ancestor?
questions.command: Inherited units always convert after their ancestors (C8CHAIN): adding a unit offers every ancestor that still holds a From type, root first, and Convert asks to reorder the list ancestor-first (No runs nothing). An unconverted ancestor that is not in the run blocks too: Yes adds the missing ancestors root-first and runs, No cancels the whole run. An ancestor class found in neither the project index nor the platform library index blocks the run: add its unit to the .dproj/.dpr and reindex. A class declared in more than one project unit is ambiguous and blocks with its own message: remove the duplicate or qualify the class. When the platform library cannot be asked, only TForm, TFrame, TDataModule and their TCustom* forms still count as library roots

entries.title: Circular Uses Report (cycles + fix plan)
entries.summary: Finds uses cycles among indexed units and, on request, proposes a followable refactoring plan to break them
entries.intro: Read this when the compiler complains about circular references or a project dependency graph feels tangled. It finds uses cycles among indexed units (--f2047 narrows to the interface-only ones dcc rejects) and, on request, writes a refactoring playbook per group: what moves, the uses edits, the new-unit text and the predicted result, plus the exact cycles --fix commands that make the mechanical part for you. Where the playbook cannot cut a cycle it says so per edge and names the reason.

steps: Choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Circular Uses Report (cycles + fix plan)...

surfaces.usage: drag-lint cycles --db <file.sqlite> [--edges] [--causes] [--hub] [--plan [--no-hub-surface | --hub-surface] [--apply] [--project <X.dproj>]] [--f2047 [--unit <stem>]] [--fix --project <X.dproj> [--hub-surface | --no-hub-surface] [--stall-exit-min <minutes>] [--cycle <n> | --unit <stem>] [--part a|b|all] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--no-reindex] [--no-compile] [--shadow-out <dir>] [--rsvars <path>] [--build-timeout <s>]] [--ctor-wide] [--format json|text] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--platform win32|win64] [--rules-dir <dir>] (circular unit deps; --hub = per group its hub units (removal leaves the rest acyclic): edges, ref weights and surfaces per side, dead uses; read-only, no planner; --f2047 = only the interface-only cycles dcc rejects with F2047, each edge with its forcing symbols and the next --plan / --fix commands; --plan = mechanical refactoring playbook: moves, uses edits, new-unit text, checklist + predicted output, and a "Fix it" block per group naming the exact --fix dry-run and --apply commands; --ctor-wide = the wider constructor-inversion whitelist for --plan / --fix (off by default); --fix = the mechanical fix of one group, see the cycles-fix entry)
help: drag-lint cycles             --db <file.sqlite>    [--edges] [--causes] [--hub] [--plan [--no-hub-surface | --hub-surface] [--apply] [--project <X.dproj>]] [--f2047 [--unit <stem>]] [--fix --project <X.dproj> [--hub-surface | --no-hub-surface] [--stall-exit-min <minutes>] [--cycle <n> | --unit <stem>] [--part a|b|all] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--no-reindex] [--no-compile] [--shadow-out <dir>] [--rsvars <path>] [--build-timeout <s>]] [--ctor-wide] [--format json|text] [--library-db <lib.sqlite>] [--platform win32|win64] [--rules-dir <dir>]   (circular unit deps; --hub = per group its hub units (removal leaves the rest acyclic): edges, ref weights and surfaces per side, dead uses; read-only, no planner; --f2047 = only the interface-only cycles dcc rejects with F2047: units, each interface edge with the symbols forcing it, and the next --plan / --fix commands; --unit <stem> (the name in dcc's message) narrows it, a unit in no such cycle is exit 0 with a note; --format json = [{units[],edges[{from,to,symbols[]}],plan,fix}]; --ctor-wide = the wider constructor-inversion whitelist for --plan / --fix (off by default); --fix = the mechanical cycle fix for ONE group (the first mechanical one, or --cycle / --unit; text names the groups it did not plan): dry run = verdict + cycle-fix/1 JSON, no source written, stages the result in a shadow tree (default C:\TEMP\draglint_cyclefix_<pid>\, deleted at exit unless a message of the run cites a file in it, then kept and named on stderr; --shadow-out names another, never deleted) and builds the project (msbuild /p:Config=Debug for --platform, default the project's active platform, else win32) unless --no-compile, exit 0 mechanical / 1 refused / 2 error; --apply writes it (.BCK<n> backups unless --no-backup), builds, re-indexes unless --no-reindex and re-runs cycles against the prediction, exit 0 written and verified (or written with --no-reindex, unverified) / 1 refused, rolled back after a compile error or build timeout, or written but not verified / 2 error: a write or build failed part-way (rolled back, project not changed, or the rollback failure is named) or bad flags; a rollback restores the sources, not the DCUs the failed build wrote: rebuild after a rollback; --apply --no-compile is exit 2; --rsvars <path> = the Studio build environment the compile gate calls (default: the Studio the registry or BDS names; forwarded to every --part all iteration; a missing file is exit 2); --build-timeout <s> = whole seconds one build may take (default 0 = no limit; forwarded to every --part all iteration; anything but a whole number >= 0 is exit 2); a stand-down request (drag-lint shutdown --db <db>, or the IDE's Cancel) kills the build, rolls an --apply back and exits 1 ("cancelled -- rolled back"); --part all needs --apply, refuses --no-reindex; --plan = mechanical refactoring playbook: moves, uses edits, new-unit text, checklist + predicted output, and a "Fix it" block per group (the exact --fix dry-run and --apply commands; --project names the project in them, else <your.dproj>); --library-db / --platform name the platform library --plan reads class ancestry from (default: the manifest's library for the build platform: --platform, else the --project's active platform, else win32; --library-db none = no library); --rules-dir is forwarded to every --part all iteration; --plan --hub-surface = recipe R3 for a group with exactly one hub read through one global (spec P2): a new leaf unit <Hub>.Hub with an interface of the members the spokes read through the global, the hub class implements it, receiver-only rewrite in the spokes, the hub's free routines through R1 pointers in <Hub>.Hub; the dry run is the playbook with R3 + the --hub block in place of Part A for such a group -- without the switch when R3 predicts that the group breaks (since 1.51 the --plan dry run; since 1.52 also --plan --apply, --fix and the --causes --format json fix object; --no-hub-surface = the planner for every group, the default before 1.52; --hub-surface = R3 also for a group it cannot break) --, --causes --format json gives R3's fix{part:r3} without the planner and names the gated cycles --fix --hub-surface dry-run / --apply commands; --fix with R3 (1.51.1) writes one group through the same compile gate as --fix: baseline build, write under .BCK<n> backups, build after the edit, rollback on a new error, re-index + verify (cycle-fix/1 part r3, recipe hub-surface; refusal hub-surface-group-stays); --plan --apply writes ONE group (.BCK<n> backups unless --no-backup) without a compile gate: build after it, or use --fix, which gates the same edit; --format json --causes adds per-group fix{available,part,dry_run,apply,edges[],reason,followup} and edges[] with each edge's surface: members read, writes, construction, class methods, routine + signature types)

entries.title: Code-built menu tree and registry drift
entries.summary: The menu tree a Delphi program builds in code, read statically, and a check that the registered menu paths still match it
entries.intro: Read this when a menu is built in code (TMenuItem.Create, Caption :=, Add) rather than in a .dfm and you need to see the real tree, or when a documented menu path may have drifted from the code. `drag-lint menu-tree --project <dproj> --db <db>` prints the tree: helpers are recognised by what their body does, not by their name, and a caption it cannot evaluate is shown as dynamic with a note instead of being dropped. Needs a fresh project index; a changed file is refused with exit 3.
