help: drag-lint menu-tree --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> [--root <QName>] [--with-dfm] [--format text|json|paths] [--json] [--output <f>]   (the menu tree a program BUILDS IN CODE, read statically: helpers recognised by body, click wrappers, callbacks, const-array / case captions; a caption it cannot evaluate is a dynamic node + a note; --with-dfm adds the .dfm menus (DevExpress bars / ribbon / backstage / bar popups, VCL TMainMenu / TPopupMenu) as roots with the code-added links grafted in; exit 0 ran, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)

surfaces.usage: drag-lint menu-drift --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --registry <features dir> [--with-dfm] [--format text|json] [--output <f>] (code-built menu tree vs the registry's ide-menu paths and app-menu (form, path) surfaces, which imply --with-dfm; --registry defaults to <project>\_D-RAG\menu-registry: missing / moved / unregistered / notes; exit 0 no drift, 1 drift, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)
help: drag-lint menu-drift --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --registry <features dir> [--with-dfm] [--format text|json] [--json] [--output <f>]   (the code-built menu tree (+ the .dfm menus with --with-dfm) vs the registry's ide-menu PATHS and app-menu (form, path) surfaces -- an app-menu surface implies --with-dfm; --registry defaults to <project>\_D-RAG\menu-registry: MISSING (renamed? hint), MOVED (now at), UNREGISTERED (skeleton surface), NOTE; exit 0 no drift, 1 drift, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)

A cycle it cannot cut is refused with one line per reason, never half-written. --rsvars names the Studio build environment.

--format sarif            emit SARIF 2.1.0 (in addition to text|json)
--fail-on <level>         exit nonzero iff a surviving finding is >= error|warning|info|hint (none: always 0).
Without it ANY surviving finding exits 1 (= --fail-on hint); only a clean run exits 0.
--config <file>           drag-lint-lint.json (else the nearest one above --project / the file / the --db, then above the project the --db was indexed from, then the CWD)
--enable id1,id2          re-include disabled / off-by-default rules

--profile <name>          merge a named enable/disable set from the config; built-in: cwe, cert, misra, cwe-top25 (rules labelled under that standard, severity floor warning; a config profile of the same name wins)

--target-compiler <v>     index: the Delphi the PREPROCESSOR describes (VER<N>0, CompilerVersion, RTLVersion; default: --project's ProjectVersion (index --all: each section's own .dproj), then the installed RAD Studio, then 37). lint / lint-all / rules / lsp: the oldest compiler the code must compile on -- 13, 12, 11, 10.4, 10.3, XE7 ..., a CompilerVersion (37, 36 ...) or auto (the .dproj ProjectVersion); modernize findings whose fix needs a newer compiler are not reported; default 37 = Delphi 13 (config key target_compiler, profile-overridable)

entries.title: Engine heartbeat: the IDE tells a busy engine from a stuck one
entries.summary: A running engine reports what it is doing, so the IDE kills only an engine whose status stopped moving
entries.intro: Read this to understand why a long index or lint-all no longer gets killed while it works, and why a frozen engine still is. The engine keeps a status record (action, step, n of total) and answers it on a status-only pipe, drag-lint-beat-*, next to the control pipe. The IDE plugin polls it every two seconds: a changing record counts as progress, a frozen record on a spinning process counts as stuck. The status bar shows it, e.g. 'index parse 120/400'. An old engine or a verb without a beat falls back to the earlier output-or-CPU rule.

entries.title: ide-release
entries.summary: Asks a running drag-lint Delphi IDE plugin not to respawn its drag-lint.exe child processes for a while -- and to drop the running one on its next request
entries.intro: Read this when an engine build fails to copy drag-lint.exe because the Delphi IDE is open. ide-release writes a hold (--seconds N, 1 to 3600; 0, a negative number or no flag gives the default 120 s, and anything above 3600 is cut to 3600) so the plugin stops respawning the engine; --resume clears it and --status reports it. It frees nothing by itself.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint ide-release [--seconds N] [--resume] [--status] [--json] (writes a hold sentinel: a running Delphi IDE plugin will not respawn drag-lint.exe while it lasts and stops its LSP child on the next request that wants it, so the engine binary can be rebuilt while the IDE stays open; default 120s, --resume clears it early. Frees nothing by itself -- build\stage-engine.ps1 kills the running holder and retries. The plugin job queue also DEFERS its heavy jobs for the duration rather than starting them)
help: drag-lint ide-release [--seconds N] [--resume] [--status] [--json]   (writes a hold sentinel: a running Delphi IDE plugin will not respawn drag-lint.exe while it lasts and stops its LSP child on the next request that wants it, so the engine binary can be rebuilt while the IDE stays open; default 120s, --resume clears it early. entries.title: lsp
entries.summary: Starts the LSP (Language Server Protocol) stdio server
entries.intro: Read this when you want hover, completion, go-to-definition and diagnostics in an editor other than RAD Studio. It starts the language server over stdio; the IDE plugin launches it by itself, and it is not the same as the MCP server (serve) used by AI clients.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint lsp --db <file.sqlite> (LSP stdio server) [--stdio] [--parent-pid <n>] [--clientProcessId <n>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>]
help: drag-lint lsp                --db <file.sqlite>    (LSP stdio server) [--stdio] [--parent-pid <n>] [--clientProcessId <n>] [--target-compiler <ver|auto>]
--stdio and --clientProcessId are accepted and IGNORED -- editor clients pass them;
stdio is the only transport, and --parent-pid is the shutdown watch that DOES act.
in lsp mode the engine also listens on a per-user maintenance pipe -- see `drag-lint shutdown`.

--proxy [--delphi-lsp <path>] [--trace <file>] [--merge-diagnostics] [--merge-completion] [--merge-hover] [--merge-definition] [--merge-navigation] [--merge-budget-ms <n>] [--delphi-lsp-bits 32|64]: relay in front of RAD Studio's DelphiLSP,
so registering drag-lint as the Code Insight server keeps the compiler front end.
--trace appends every relayed LSP message to <file> with a direction tag (C>S / S>C); off by default.
--merge-diagnostics: append drag-lint's lint findings to DelphiLSP's publishDiagnostics (one notification, source-tagged); OFF by default.
--merge-completion: union drag-lint's completion items into DelphiLSP's reply, keyed on (label, kind); DelphiLSP's items first; OFF by default.
--merge-hover: append drag-lint's hover facts to DelphiLSP's hover after a --- rule, or answer with them alone when DelphiLSP has none; OFF by default.
--merge-definition: drag-lint's definition when DelphiLSP's is null or empty; answer references and workspace/symbol in the proxy (DelphiLSP has neither); OFF by default.
--merge-navigation: answer type and call hierarchy, typeDefinition, documentHighlight and foldingRange in the proxy, for each of those providers DelphiLSP does not advertise; OFF by default.
--merge-budget-ms <n>: per-frame budget for a merge handler; over budget forwards DelphiLSP's bytes untouched (default 300).
--delphi-lsp-bits 32|64: which DelphiLSP the proxy spawns (64 = bin64\DelphiLSP.exe, the default; 32 = bin\DelphiLSP.exe); --delphi-lsp <path> wins over it.
--full-rules: run the FULL rule set (built-ins included) out-of-process on every didSave and publish the complete finding set; OFF by default -- costs one `lint` run per save, reported on stderr.
drag-lint index <dir> --db <file.sqlite> --resolve-only   (re-derive call edges / ancestry / helpers / purity verdicts from the STORED parses; skips the walk entirely --
the cheap remedy when resolver_fingerprint says the edges are stale, since no parse became wrong)
ONLY safe if no source changed since the parse: a changed file is WITHHELD, and after the clear this pass runs it HAS NO EDGES OR MEMBER ACCESSES until a plain index
it writes edges INSIDE this one index only -- no cross-store edges are written (measured
2026-09-22: 0 refs.external_target in every project DB; re-resolving the libraries under
resolver 1.5.1 added 13 intra-library edges per platform, and nothing across stores)
drag-lint index --project <file.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --resolve-only   (the same, for a PROJECT database -- the form
to type there: without --resolve-only the <dir> form above widens a project DB into a folder DB)

a DB resolved against a library and re-resolved with no library store attached warns on stderr (WARNING: index: no library store attached: library bindings are kept from the last library run, not refreshed; pass --library-db <library.sqlite>) and keeps the stored bindings (1.52; 1.51.1 cleared them).
drag-lint index --all --resolve-only   (the same, across every manifest section -- the only command that reaches them all;
use it to repair indexes stamped by a build that skipped the pass, which no later build can detect)

library-first resolve: a section with libraryResolve whose platform library is not READY (missing, rebuilding, stale extractor) is resolved without it; the run marks the DB pending (schema_meta library_resolve_state) and says on stderr that the result is INCOMPLETE. The next index run re-resolves it once the library is ready, no flag needed.

entries.title: Field repository: generated handlers
entries.summary: Writes the field repository's event code and MAXLEN constants into hash-checked DLFR regions of existing units
entries.intro: Read this when calculated-field and field-event code, or MAXLEN constants, should come from the field repository. A region edited by hand is reported and never overwritten; everything outside the regions is kept byte for byte.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint repo <gen-handlers|gen-maxlen|renumber-regions> (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--dfm <file.dfm>[;...]] [--dataset <Name>] [--code-dir <folder>] [--table <T,...>] [--in <file.pas>[;...]] [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json]
help: drag-lint repo gen-handlers   --dfm <file.dfm>[;...] [--dataset <Name>] (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json]   (writes the stored event code of a form's datasets (OnCalcFields, OnGetText, OnSetText, OnValidate, OnChange) into the handlers the DFM assigns, as hash-checked DLFR regions; a region edited by hand is refused and kept; a body that reads another table ({{ALIAS.FIELD}}) is refused until its SQL is composed; needs a schema-4 repository; everything outside the regions stays byte for byte; no --apply = dry run; exit 1 a region or unit refused or not written, 2 usage)

drag-lint repo gen-maxlen     --code-dir <folder> [--table <T,...>] (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json]   (writes the <TABLE>_<FIELD>_MAXLEN constants into region DLFR 2a of each interface unit i<TABLE>.pas; no --apply = dry run; exit codes as gen-handlers)

drag-lint repo renumber-regions (--code-dir <folder> | --in <file.pas>[;...]) (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json]   (renames the numbered ORM region markers DB-RAD n to DLFR n, whole units only; update-orm reads both; no --apply = dry run; exit codes as gen-handlers)

entries.title: Field repository
entries.summary: Keeps the TableTools field registry in one SQLite file per database, filled from Firebird (read-only), with a diffable text backup
entries.intro: Read this when you want the TableTools field repository without Firebird tables or the TableTools IDE package. Run drag-lint repo init, then repo import-fb (Micronite) or repo seed-fb (any Firebird database), keep the text backup in version control with repo backup, and point several projects at one repository with the fieldRepository key. Firebird is never modified.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Open Field Repository Editor...
steps: Open a project that has a field repository (fieldRepository key or the default file)
Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Open Field Repository Editor...
The grid editor dl-field-repo.exe opens on that repository

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Refresh Schema from Database...
steps: Open a project with a field repository
Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Refresh Schema from Database...
Enter the Firebird connection string; the output of drag-lint repo refresh-schema is shown

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > FDMemTable from CSV...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > FDMemTable from CSV...
Pick a field-definition CSV
The Pascal source is written next to the CSV as `<name>.memtable.pas`

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Generate / Update ORM Source...
steps: Open the project whose field repository describes the tables
Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Generate / Update ORM Source...
Pick the folder of the `i<T>`/`u<T>` units; give table names for NEW units, or leave it empty to update the DB-RAD regions of every existing unit (optionally also the _SERVER/_CLIENT folders)
Read the dry-run summary and answer Yes to write (repo gen-orm / update-orm --apply)

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Generate DataService Units...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Generate DataService Units...
Give the table names, then pick the _SERVER and _CLIENT folders
Read the dry-run summary and answer Yes to write (repo gen-dataservice --apply); add the listed units to the projects

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Param Array Assistant...
steps: Open and save the form unit
Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Param Array Assistant...
Answer whether to prepare the queries first (--prepare-queries)
Read the --plan summary and answer Yes to write through the compile gate (repo gen-param-array --apply)

surfaces.usage: drag-lint repo <init|info|import-fb|seed-fb|refresh-schema|backup|restore|gen-memtable|gen-param-array|gen-orm|update-orm|upgrade-orm-headers|gen-dataservice|migrate|check|paths|gen-const|check-const|read-dfm> (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--connection "<Firebird connection string>"] [--ddl <file.sql>[;...]] [--select <file>] [--in <file>] [--output <file>] [--name <Name>] [--replace] [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json] [--unit <UnitName>] [--datamodule <Name>] [--unit-file <file.pas>] [--dfm <file.dfm>[;...]] [--dataset <Name>] [--direction dfm-to-repo] [--from <table>] [--to <table>] [--depth <n>] [--stats]   (the field repository: one SQLite file per database; Firebird is only read; gen-param-array needs no repository)
help: drag-lint repo init           (--repo <file> | --project <project file>)   (create an empty field repository; exit 1 when the file exists)
drag-lint repo info           (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--json|--format json]   (path, schema version, rows per table, DL_META keys; exit 1 when not a repository)

drag-lint repo import-fb      --connection "<Firebird connection string>" (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--replace]   (copy the FIB$ registry tables; ALIGNMENT -2 becomes NULL; read-only on Firebird; --replace writes a before-import text backup first; exit 1 failure, 2 schema drift)

drag-lint repo seed-fb        (--connection "<Firebird connection string>" | --ddl <file.sql>[;...]) (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply | --select <id file>] [--json]   (fill an EMPTY repository from the Firebird schema or a DDL script; prints the change set and writes nothing unless --apply or --select; read-only on Firebird)

drag-lint repo refresh-schema (--connection "<Firebird connection string>" | --ddl <file.sql>[;...]) (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply | --select <id file>] [--json]   (re-read the schema into a filled repository as a change set: new and changed values are checked, vanished ones are unchecked deletes; hand-edited columns are never touched; no --apply = dry run; --select <id file> writes exactly the listed ids)

drag-lint repo backup         (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--output <file>]   (write the diffable text backup of the field repository; default <repo>.txt; a backup of the DATABASE is repo backup --connection)

drag-lint repo restore        --in <backup file> (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--replace]   (create the repository when missing; a malformed backup prints "line <n>: ..." and exits 2, nothing changed)
drag-lint repo gen-memtable   --in <csv file> [--name <Name>] [--output <file>]   (Pascal source that builds the fields of a TFDMemTable from a field-definition CSV; exit 2 on a bad CSV)

drag-lint repo gen-param-array (--in [--dfm ] | --project --all [--only ]) [--query ] [--table ] [--step-size ] [--progress-form
] [--prepare-queries] [--plan | --apply --project [--no-backup] [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ]] [--json] (FireDAC Array-DML loop from the unit's DFM, inserted as a braced comment before the final end.; no flag prints the block, --plan the diff, --apply writes through ONE compile gate; --prepare-queries first does the IDE assistant's query preparation (each SELECT TFDQuery gets its TFDUpdateSQL INSERT SQL, ObjectView=False, no CachedUpdates; update object / schema adapter renamed ZZZ*, persistent fields removed with their declarations; .dfm + .pas diffs in --plan, both written through the gate); exit 1 a unit refused or no block, 2 bad flags or a baseline that does not build)

drag-lint repo gen-orm        (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) --code-dir <folder> [--table <T,...>] [--apply [--no-backup]]   (new i<T>.PAS + u<T>.PAS ORM units per repository table; dry run prints the diff, --apply writes 7-bit ASCII, an existing file is first copied to <file>.BCKn; prints add to project: per new file)

drag-lint repo update-orm     (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) --code-dir <folder> [--server-dir <folder>] [--client-dir <folder>] [--table <T,...>] [--save-form legacy|current] [--overwrite-edited <id,...|all>] [--apply [--no-backup]]   (rewrites ONLY the DB-RAD regions of the existing i/u/_SERVER/_CLIENT units, every other byte kept; a region of an id it does not generate (DB-RAD 99) is hand code and kept; a unit whose markers cannot be trusted is REFUSED and left unchanged, the others are written, exit 1 with --apply (a dry run lists them, exit 0); each regenerated start marker carries the hash of its body (a legacy marker gets one on its first write), and a region whose body no longer matches its hash is hand-edited: kept and listed as REFUSED region (exit 1 with --apply) unless --overwrite-edited names it or all, or you answer YES at the console question (asked only when stdin is a console); --save-form legacy (default) = the FIELD_AS_TYPE parameter binding the ORM3 units carry, current = TableTools 2026-05-19 .Value / .AsWideMemo / Set1Byte / NULL-timestamp Clear)

drag-lint repo upgrade-orm-headers (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) --code-dir <folder> [--table <T,...>] [--apply [--no-backup]]   (one-time, 1.54: replaces the generated with-header of Assign / AssignTo and the unused Reader locals in the existing u<T> units, and AssignI by the overloaded Assign in each i<T> + u<T> pair (both units or neither); dry-run diff unless --apply; a hand-edited header or pair is listed and left alone; every remaining call of AssignI is listed as file(line) and never edited; run repo update-orm as well, it rewrites the regions)

drag-lint repo gen-dataservice (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) --server-dir <folder> --client-dir <folder> [--table <T,...>] [--save-form legacy|current] [--apply [--no-backup]]   (new u<T>_SERVER.PAS + u<T>_CLIENT.PAS per table and the two DI container units; prints add to project: per new file)

drag-lint repo migrate        (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply]   (schema 1, 2 or 3 -> 4: adds DL_RELATIONS, DL_RELATION_COLUMNS and DL_FIELD_INPUTS (cross-table fields), from schema 2 also the event columns of DL_FIELDS_INFO and DL_GRID_COLUMNS, from schema 1 also CALC_BODY, DL_LAYOUT_EVENTS, DL_EXCEPTIONS, the schema-fact tables and FIELD_KIND 2 for ISCALCULATED rows; ALIGNMENT -2 becomes NULL; no --apply = dry run that changes no byte; --apply writes <repo>.before-migrate-<yyyymmdd-hhnnss>.txt first; a schema-4 file prints already at schema 4)

drag-lint repo check          (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--json]   (read-only: FIELD_KIND vs ISCALCULATED/ISLOOKUP, lookup wiring, calc and event macros, dependency cycles, ALIGNMENT, layout-event and grid-column rows; schema 4: {{ALIAS.FIELD}} inputs, their paths and bindings, relations and their parent keys; exit 0 clean, 1 findings)

drag-lint repo paths          (--from <table> --to <table> | --stats) [--depth <n>] (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--json]   (read-only, 1.55: the relation paths from a home table UP to a parent table within --depth steps (default 3): FKs onto a PK / UNIQUE of the schema facts plus confirmed FORM / HAND relations; a parent with no key is never an edge; each path with its default input alias (TABLE, TABLE_2, ...) and the rule that chooses it: stored IS_DEFAULT, exactly one path, or ambiguous (asked once, never chosen by data); --stats instead counts the reachable and ambiguous table pairs at depth 1..n; exit 0 listed, 1 no path, 2 usage)

drag-lint repo gen-const      (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--unit <UnitName>] --output <file.pas> [--table <T,...>] [--datamodule <Name>] [--dry-run]   (the repository as ONE read-only Pascal unit shared by SERVER and CLIENT: constant record arrays per table; with --datamodule <Name> instead a data module unit plus its .dfm whose TFDMemTables open PRE-FILLED and read only, no fill code; default tables DL_FIELDS_INFO, DL_DATASETS_INFO, DL_ENUMVALUES, DL_ERROR_MESSAGES; writes only --output and the .dfm beside it; exit 2 on a bad --table / --unit / --datamodule / --output)

drag-lint repo check-const    (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) --unit-file <file.pas>   (does a unit written by gen-const still match the repository? exit 0 current, 1 stale naming the changed tables or the edited form, 2 the check could not be made; a pre-build step)

drag-lint repo read-dfm       --dfm <file.dfm>[;...] [--dataset <Name>] --direction dfm-to-repo (--repo <file> | --project <project file>) [--apply | --select <id file>] [--dry-run] [--json]   (the persistent fields of a form's datasets as a change set: data, calc, lookup, internal-calc and aggregate fields, captions / formats / widths, lookup wiring, OnCalcFields code as CALC_BODY with {{FIELD}} component macros, OnGetText / OnSetText / OnValidate / OnChange code and OnGetDisplayText / OnCustomDrawCell code of TcxGridDBTableView columns, the column order of table and banded grid views (DL_GRID_COLUMNS); code in generated DLFR regions is not read back; needs a schema-4 repository; text or binary DFM, BDE or FireDAC; the table comes from UpdateTableName, TableName or a one-table SELECT, a join gives every field its own table, a calc reading several tables goes to the child end with {{ALIAS.FIELD}} inputs (alias = the table name) and DL_FIELD_INPUTS / DL_RELATIONS rows (the form's ON / WHERE joins choose the path; a join on a parent key with no FK is offered as a FORM relation, unchecked), a memory table takes the source of its AttachedTo or of a literal AttachTable / CloneCursor / CopyDataSet / CopyData / AppendData / Data := (cycle or two sources = unresolved), anything else is listed as UNRESOLVED; with --dataset --json also lists the persistent fields and the repository fields of the table; no --apply = dry run; exit 1 read / apply failure, 2 usage or a bad --select file)

entries.title: stop-now
entries.summary: Ask running engines (lsp, cycles --fix, index, lint-all) to stand down cleanly, so an index can be rebuilt or an engine replaced
entries.intro: Read this when you need to rebuild an index that running engines hold open, or replace a running engine: stop-now asks the running engines (lsp, cycles --fix, and the long index and lint-all runs) to close their stores and stand down, without killing them (only --force terminates an engine that does not answer). An index run stops between files with its database consistent and the same command resumes; the installer and build\stage-engine.ps1 use this channel first.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint stop-now [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force] (ask running engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0; `index` and `lint-all` runs exit 4)
help: drag-lint stop-now [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force]   (ask running engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0; `index` and `lint-all` runs exit 4)
transport: a Windows NAMED PIPE, never a TCP port -- \\.\pipe\drag-lint-ctl-<sid>-s<session>-p<pid>, created with an
explicit DACL for the creating user only, so another user or session cannot signal your engines. Engines in

`lsp`, `cycles --fix`, `index` (incl. --all), `lint-all` and `warm-rule-cache` mode listen (`serve` and other one-shot verbs do not): an index run stops between files, database consistent, same command resumes; lint-all prints PARTIAL findings; a warm stops at once (exit 4). --all (the default) asks every
reachable engine; --db keeps only engines holding that index; --dry-run lists them and changes nothing.
--wait (default 5 s) bounds the graceful wait per engine: one inside a request answers BUSY and keeps
running (exit 1). --force TerminateProcess'es ONLY an engine that refused or did not answer, and says
ESCALATING when it does. Every honoured or refused request is audited on the engine's stderr and in
%LOCALAPPDATA%\drag-lint\control-channel-audit.log (who asked: pid + exe, when).
